question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of registered unemployed persons in Germany in October 2026 (not seasonally adjusted, all of Germany), as it will be first reported in the Federal Employment Agency's (Bundesagentur für Arbeit) monthly labour market press release.

target.what: Registered unemployed persons in Germany (Arbeitslose) as reported in the Bundesagentur für Arbeit monthly labour market press release, national total, not seasonally adjusted, stock at the reference date of the October 2026 reporting month
target.publisher: Bundesagentur für Arbeit (Federal Employment Agency), Statistik der BA
target.cadence: monthly, published in a press release around the end of the reporting month or the first days of the following month
target.caveats: The BA reports the unemployment stock as a monthly figure referring to a reference date (Monatsende/Zähltag) within the reporting month, not a monthly average; the press release figure is the national not-seasonally-adjusted total. The October 2026 figure will be published around late October/early

candidates.perspective: BA monthly labour market statistics time series
candidates.hypothesis: October unadjusted unemployment stock follows a stable seasonal pattern relative to September and to the prior October; the target equals the most recent observed level plus the typical September-to-October seasonal change plus a trend/cycle adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: BA monthly national unemployment stock (Arbeitslose, nicht saisonbereinigt) for all months from 2023 through the latest month published before 2026-10-19 (likely August or September 2026), plus October values for 2023, 2024, 2025 and the September-to-October month-on-month changes in those years.

candidates.perspective: BA press releases and monthly reports for the most recent months before cutoff
candidates.hypothesis: The latest published monthly level and its reported month-on-month change give the base level; applying the historical average September-to-October seasonal increment yields the October 2026 estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Headline unemployment stock and month-on-month change from BA press releases for July, August and September 2026 (if published before 2026-10-19), plus the BA's own commentary on trend direction (increase/decrease) in those releases.
search_hints: Bundesagentur für Arbeit Pressemitteilung September 2026 Arbeitslose

candidates.perspective: Eurostat / OECD harmonised unemployment series for Germany
candidates.hypothesis: Harmonised unemployment (ILO definition) levels and month-on-month changes for Germany track the registered series with a roughly stable ratio; the ratio can bridge from a harmonised estimate to the registered stock.
candidates.data_to_find: Eurostat une_rt_m or OECD harmonised unemployment level for Germany (thousands, seasonally adjusted and unadjusted) for months up to the latest available before 2026-10-19, and the historical ratio of registered BA unemployment to harmonised unemployment for October months.
search_hints: Germany registered unemployed vs ILO unemployed ratio

candidates.perspective: Economic research institutes, Bundesbank, and consensus forecasters
candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts of German unemployment for late 2026 (levels or rates) constrain the October 2026 stock; converting a forecast unemployment rate via labour force gives an independent estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Autumn 2026 joint economic forecast (Gemeinschaftsdiagnose), Bundesbank Monthly Report, ifo/IAB labour market forecasts, and any consensus for German unemployment in Q4 2026, expressed as level or rate, published before 2026-10-19.

candidates.perspective: Labour market flow accounting (BA Arbeitsmarkt in Zahlen)
candidates.hypothesis: The stock equals the previous stock plus inflows (Zugänge in Arbeitslosigkeit) minus outflows (Abgänge aus Arbeitslosigkeit); October inflows rise seasonally as summer jobs and training contracts end, so the net flow is typically positive.
candidates.data_to_find: BA monthly gross flows: Zugänge in und Abgänge aus Arbeitslosigkeit, and the stock, for recent months and October months of prior years, to estimate the typical October net flow.
search_hints: Arbeitsmarkt in Zahlen Zu- und Abgänge Arbeitslosigkeit Oktober

candidates.perspective: BA short-time work, job vacancies, and registration statistics
candidates.hypothesis: Rising short-time work (Kurzarbeit) and falling vacancies signal weakening demand and upward pressure on unemployment; the direction and magnitude of recent changes inform the trend adjustment to the seasonal baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: BA reported Kurzarbeit (Anzeigen und realisierte Kurzarbeit) and gemeldete Arbeitsstellen for mid-2026, plus their recent trends, to gauge whether October 2026 sits above or below the seasonal baseline.

candidates.perspective: Seasonal adjustment factors and calendar effects
candidates.hypothesis: The unadjusted October figure equals the seasonally adjusted level times a seasonal factor; BA/ Eurostat seasonal factors for October are stable and can convert an adjusted-level estimate into the unadjusted target.
candidates.data_to_find: BA or Eurostat seasonal adjustment factors / seasonal components for German unemployment for October, and the latest seasonally adjusted unemployment level for 2026, to reconstruct the unadjusted October value.
search_hints: Eurostat seasonal adjustment unemployment Germany October factor

candidates.perspective: Macro and policy shocks affecting German labour demand in 2026
candidates.hypothesis: Specific shocks (industrial restructuring, automotive sector layoffs, energy prices, migration/refugee labour supply, policy changes) shift October 2026 away from the pure seasonal extrapolation; measurable exposure indicates the sign and rough size of the deviation.
candidates.data_to_find: Documented 2026 layoff announcements, restructuring events, migration/Ukraine refugee labour market integration figures, and any policy changes (e.g. Bürgergeld reform) affecting registration, dated before 2026-10-19.

methods.rationale: Seasonal extrapolation: take the latest observed September 2026 level (2,994,000, p11/p146) and add the typical September-to-October seasonal change. The seasonal change is anchored on the 2025 observation (p20/p71/p86 minus p25/p76/p91) and widened for year-to-year variation. Main failure mode: the 2026 seasonal pattern differs from 2025, or the labour-market weakening offsets the seasonal decline.

methods.rationale: Year-on-year route: October 2025 level (2,911,000, p20/p71/p86) plus the expected year-on-year change, anchored on the September 2026 y/y change of +40,000 (p1/p34/p157) and August +36,000 (p41/p62). Main failure mode: the y/y trend shifts sharply in October 2026.

assumptions.name: September-to-October 2026 unadjusted change in national registered unemployed, as a factor on the observed 2025 step
assumptions.rationale: Only one observed September-to-October step exists (p20/p221: -44,000 in 2025). October usually brings a small decline as summer-job and training-contract inflows fade. The 2026 labour market is slightly weaker (y/y +40,000 in September, p1; adjusted drift +12,000, p4), so the decline is assumed marginally smaller in magnitude than 2025, i.e. a factor near 0.9 on the -44,000 step. Range spans a near-flat October (factor 0.4) to a steeper decline than 2025 (factor 1.6).
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 September-to-October seasonal pattern resembles 2025 and no large shock hits in October.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that October 2026 inflows from training-contract endings are unusually large, or a BA statement of a rising October stock.

assumptions.name: Year-on-year change in national unadjusted registered unemployed, October 2026 vs October 2025, as a factor on the observed September 2026 y/y change

assumptions.applies_when: The y/y trend of late summer 2026 persists into October.
assumptions.falsified_by: A sharp autumn 2026 deterioration or improvement in the adjusted series (e.g. adjusted change far outside +1,000 to +20,000).

methods.label: m1

p11.role: September 2026 national unadjusted registered unemployed stock (level, persons)

p20.role: September-to-October 2025 unadjusted change in national registered unemployed (signed persons, -44,000), used as the seasonal step template

a1.role: dimensionless factor scaling the 2025 September-to-October step to October 2026

methods.rationale: Own-history seasonal route: latest observed unadjusted level (2,994,415 in September 2026, p11) plus the 2025 September-to-October step (p20, -44,000) scaled by a factor a1 near 0.9. The step is the largest uncertainty because only 2025 is observed; the factor range reflects that. Shared dependency: p11 and p20 both derive from BA monthly data.
methods.error: input p11 must be positive for lognormal sampling

methods.label: m2

p20.role: October 2025 national unadjusted registered unemployed stock (level, persons)

p1.role: September 2026 year-on-year change in national registered unemployed (+40,000 persons), used as the y/y trend anchor

a2.role: dimensionless factor scaling the September 2026 y/y change to the October 2026 y/y change

methods.rationale: Year-on-year route: October 2025 level (2,911,000, p20) plus the October 2026 y/y change, anchored on the September 2026 y/y change (+40,000, p1) and scaled by a2 near 1.0 to reflect the mild positive adjusted drift. Independent of the September-to-October step assumption, so it diversifies m1's main failure mode.
methods.error: input p20 must be positive for lognormal sampling

kept.rationale: Only one observed September-to-October step exists (p20/p221: -44,000 in 2025). October usually brings a small decline as summer-job and training-contract inflows fade. kept.applies_when: The 2026 September-to-October seasonal pattern resembles 2025 and no large shock hits in October.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that October 2026 inflows from training-contract endings are unusually large, or a BA statement of a rising October stock.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
